exposure: Early prophylactic intravenous ampicillin prior to catheter balloon insertion
Routine intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) at onset of active labor or rupture of membranes
cohort: The cohort consisted of 144 patients with term singleton pregnancies undergoing induction of labor for medical indications, who had Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonization, at two tertiary medical centers.
finding: Prophylactic antibiotics administered prior to catheter balloon insertion in GBS-colonized patients undergoing induction of labor were associated with a significantly lower risk of clinical chorioamnionitis and maternal fever.
mod_finding: No statistically significant differences were observed in cesarean delivery rates between the early prophylactic antibiotics group and the routine IAP group.
